intent.raw_query: Costa Rica eco-adventure, $2500, zip-lining and wildlife, February 2026 from Miami

experiences.name: Monteverde Cloud Forest Zip-Line Canopy Tour
experiences.description: Soar through the misty cloud forest canopy on one of Costa Rica's most thrilling zip-line circuits. With over 13 cables and Tarzan swings, you'll glide above the treetops spotting howler monkeys, toucans, and exotic orchids while experienced guides share insights about the unique cloud forest ecosystem.

experiences.name: Tortuguero National Park Wildlife Boat Safari
experiences.description: Navigate the jungle waterways of Tortuguero by boat with a naturalist guide to spot caimans, river otters, manatees, three-toed sloths, and hundreds of bird species. If visiting between July and October, witness the awe-inspiring nesting of green sea turtles on the black-sand beaches at night.

experiences.name: Arenal Volcano Hanging Bridges & Hot Springs
experiences.description: Trek through primary rainforest on a network of suspension bridges offering panoramic views of Arenal Volcano and its surrounding wildlife. Spot poison dart frogs, coatis, and morpho butterflies by day, then unwind in natural volcanic hot spring pools fed by geothermal activity as the jungle comes alive at dusk.

experiences.name: Manuel Antonio National Park Guided Wildlife Hike
experiences.description: Explore one of the world's most biodiverse national parks with a certified naturalist guide equipped with a high-powered spotting scope. Encounter white-faced capuchin monkeys, two-toed sloths, scarlet macaws, and iguanas along jungle trails that open onto pristine white-sand beaches with turquoise Pacific waters.

experiences.name: Osa Peninsula Corcovado Jungle Expedition & Snorkeling
experiences.description: Venture into Corcovado National Park, dubbed by National Geographic as the most biologically intense place on Earth. Hike remote trails with a ranger guide to spot tapirs, peccaries, and harpy eagles, then snorkel the coral reefs of Caño Island teeming with sea turtles, reef sharks, and manta rays in the warm Pacific waters.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Costa Rica
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: No activities — flight in transit
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities — flight in transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Juan Santamaría International Airport at 22:30 on flight UA. Clear customs and immigration, collect luggage, and arrange pre-booked budget shuttle or shared transfer to Aegean Bliss Resort. Grab a light snack from the airport kiosks if needed. Check in and rest.

meals.breakfast: On the plane or airport snack
meals.lunch: On the plane or airport food court
meals.dinner: Late-night airport kiosk snack or convenience store near hotel — budget $5–8

day_by_day.notes: Pre-book a shared shuttle in advance (approx $15–25 USD) rather than a taxi to save money. Have your hotel address printed or saved offline. Exchange a small amount of colones at the airport for tips and small purchases.

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and recover from travel. After a slow start, walk the beachfront area near Aegean Bliss Resort to get oriented. Explore the immediate shoreline, watch for coastal birds like magnificent frigatebirds and brown pelicans — free wildlife watching right from the beach.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head into the nearest local town on foot or by local bus (approx $1–2 USD). Visit the local mercado (market) to pick up fresh tropical fruits like mangoes, pineapple, and papaya for cheap snacks. Stroll through town, chat with locals, and find a small soda (local Costa Rican diner) for a casado lunch.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort area. Watch the sunset from the beach — one of Costa Rica's finest free experiences. Have dinner at a nearby local soda and enjoy the relaxed beachfront atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Fruit and coffee at the hotel or nearby bakery — budget $3–5
meals.lunch: Casado (rice, beans, protein, salad) at a local soda — budget $5–8
meals.dinner: Grilled fish or chicken at a beachfront soda — budget $6–10

day_by_day.notes: A 'casado' is the quintessential budget Costa Rican meal and incredibly filling. Sodas are always cheaper than tourist restaurants. Stay hydrated — February is dry season and can be hot.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning wildlife walk along the beach and nearby mangroves or estuary (if accessible from resort). Look for howler monkeys, iguanas, and shorebirds. Bring binoculars if you have them. This is completely free and best done at sunrise when animals are most active.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrange a budget snorkeling excursion or rent snorkel gear locally (approx $10–15 USD) to explore the nearshore reef or rocky outcroppings. Alternatively, take a local bus to a nearby national park entrance for a self-guided hike on the main trail.
day_by_day.evening: Cook a simple meal using market fruits and local supermarket finds, or head to a beachside soda for a budget dinner. Enjoy the night sky on the beach — Costa Rica's skies are stunning away from city lights.

meals.breakfast: Gallo pinto (rice and beans with egg) at a local soda — budget $3–5
meals.lunch: Fresh ceviche from a beach shack or market stall — budget $4–7
meals.dinner: Rice and bean bowl with plantains at a local soda — budget $5–8

day_by_day.notes: Gallo pinto is the traditional Costa Rican breakfast and is extremely cheap and nutritious. Always apply reef-safe sunscreen before snorkeling to protect coral ecosystems.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to a nearby national park or wildlife reserve. Take a local bus or arrange a shared shuttle (budget $5–15 USD). Enter the park (entrance fees typically $18–20 USD for foreigners — worth every cent). Begin a self-guided morning hike on the main trail, watching for sloths, toucans, and howler monkeys.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring the park trails. Visit any waterfalls or river crossings on the trail route. Pack your own lunch from the market to avoid expensive park-area restaurants. Rest at a shaded viewpoint and listen to the jungle sounds.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort by local bus. Rest and freshen up. Head out for a casual dinner at a local soda near the hotel.

meals.breakfast: Packed breakfast from hotel or bakery before departure — budget $3–5
meals.lunch: Packed lunch from market: bread, cheese, fruit, water — budget $4–6
meals.dinner: Chicken or fish casado at a local soda — budget $6–9

day_by_day.notes: Wear sturdy closed-toe shoes or hiking sandals on park trails. Bring insect repellent, a rain poncho (even in dry season, microclimates vary), and at least 2 liters of water per person. Start hiking early to beat the heat.

day_by_day.morning: ZIP-LINING DAY! Book a budget zip-line tour through a local operator rather than a large resort company to save 20–40%. Many operators in Costa Rica offer multi-line canopy tours for $40–65 USD. Arrive early for the first tour slot. Soar through the rainforest canopy with stunning views of the jungle and coastline.
day_by_day.afternoon: After zip-lining, explore the surrounding area on foot. Many canopy tour operators are near forested areas where you can spot wildlife. Walk any accessible nature trails near the zip-line site for free post-tour exploration.
day_by_day.evening: Celebrate your zip-lining adventure! Treat yourself to a slightly nicer dinner — still budget-friendly but a small splurge. Look for a local restaurant with fresh seafood or traditional Costa Rican cuisine.

meals.breakfast: Hearty gallo pinto with eggs and coffee before the tour — budget $4–6
meals.lunch: Snack bar at zip-line site or packed fruit and granola bars — budget $3–5
meals.dinner: Fresh grilled fish at a local seafood restaurant — budget $10–14

day_by_day.notes: Book zip-lining in advance online or through your hotel to secure spots and sometimes get early-bird discounts. Weight and age restrictions may apply — confirm with the operator. Wear comfortable, close-toed shoes and avoid loose jewelry.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and recovery morning. Enjoy a slow beach morning — swimming, reading, or simply relaxing on the shore. Practice your wildlife spotting by watching for coastal birds, crabs, and any marine life visible from the beach.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore a nearby town or village by local bus. Visit a local artisan market or craft fair if available. Pick up handmade souvenirs like painted wooden animals, woven bags, or local coffee — negotiate prices politely. Visit a local supermarket (supermercado) to stock up on cheap snacks and water.
day_by_day.evening: Beachside bonfire or sunset gathering if permitted near the resort. Connect with other budget travelers at the hostel common area or hotel lobby. Share travel tips and potentially arrange shared costs for future excursions.

meals.breakfast: Fruit smoothie and toast at a local café — budget $4–6
meals.lunch: Empanadas or patacones (fried plantains) from a street vendor — budget $3–5
meals.dinner: Casado at a new soda you haven't tried yet — budget $5–8

day_by_day.notes: Costa Rican coffee is world-class and very cheap locally. Buy a bag of whole beans from a supermarket to take home — far cheaper than airport shops. Bartering is acceptable at artisan markets but always be respectful.

day_by_day.morning: Waterfall hike day! Research the nearest accessible waterfall (many are free or have a small $2–5 entry fee). Start early to beat the crowds and the midday heat. The hike to most waterfalls in Costa Rica is through lush jungle — prime wildlife spotting territory.
day_by_day.afternoon: Swim in the natural pool at the base of the waterfall — one of Costa Rica's most magical free (or nearly free) experiences. Have a packed picnic lunch by the waterfall. Explore the surrounding forest on any marked side trails.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort. Rinse off and relax. Head to a local soda for dinner. If energy allows, take an evening stroll along the beach to look for nesting sea turtles (if in season and in the right area) or bioluminescent plankton in the water.

meals.breakfast: Gallo pinto and fresh juice before the hike — budget $4–6
meals.lunch: Packed lunch: sandwiches, fruit, nuts, and plenty of water — budget $4–6
meals.dinner: Arroz con pollo (rice with chicken) at a local soda — budget $5–8

day_by_day.notes: Always check trail conditions before heading to waterfalls. Wear water shoes or sandals with grip for slippery rocks near the falls. Never swim directly under the waterfall due to strong currents and falling rocks.

day_by_day.morning: Wildlife-focused morning: arrange or join a budget guided wildlife tour ($20–35 USD for a group tour). Look for sloths, howler and white-faced capuchin monkeys, toucans, scarlet macaws, and caimans. A knowledgeable local guide dramatically increases your chances of spotting elusive wildlife.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a local butterfly garden or frog sanctuary if available nearby (typically $10–15 USD entry). These small eco-attractions offer incredible close-up encounters with poison dart frogs, morpho butterflies, and other exotic species in a controlled, educational setting.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset kayaking on a nearby river, estuary, or calm bay. Rent kayaks locally for $10–20 USD per hour. Paddle through mangroves at dusk for incredible bird and wildlife sightings as animals come out for the evening.

meals.breakfast: Pancakes with fresh fruit at a local café — budget $4–7
meals.lunch: Ceviche and patacones at a beachside shack — budget $5–8
meals.dinner: Vegetarian rice and beans with plantains at a soda — budget $4–7

day_by_day.notes: Early morning (6–8am) and late afternoon (4–6pm) are the best times for wildlife spotting. Wear neutral-colored clothing (greens, browns, grays) to blend into the environment and avoid startling animals.

day_by_day.morning: Surfing lesson or stand-up paddleboarding (SUP) session on the beach. Many beach towns in Costa Rica offer group surf lessons for $25–40 USD including board rental — excellent value. Even beginners can catch waves in Costa Rica's gentle beach breaks.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore tide pools along the rocky sections of the coastline during low tide. Look for sea stars, hermit crabs, sea urchins, and small fish — completely free and endlessly fascinating. Check a tide chart app before going.
day_by_day.evening: Visit a local pulpería (small corner store) and pick up ingredients for a simple beach picnic dinner. Enjoy it on the sand as the stars come out. Costa Rica has minimal light pollution in coastal areas, making stargazing exceptional.

meals.breakfast: Toast, eggs, and coffee at the hotel or nearby bakery — budget $3–5
meals.lunch: Fresh coconut water from a roadside vendor and fruit — budget $2–4
meals.dinner: Picnic: local cheese, bread, fruits, and juice from the pulpería — budget $5–8

day_by_day.notes: If surfing, always follow the instructor's safety guidelines. Never surf alone as a beginner. Apply waterproof sunscreen generously — the tropical sun is intense even on cloudy days. Bring a rash guard for UV protection.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to a nearby eco-reserve or biological station. Many research stations in Costa Rica offer public guided tours at budget prices ($15–25 USD). These offer incredible educational insights into Costa Rican biodiversity and conservation efforts alongside exceptional wildlife encounters.
day_by_day.afternoon: Participate in a volunteer or citizen science activity if available through the reserve (sometimes free in exchange for a few hours of help with reforestation or beach cleanup). This is a meaningful way to give back while traveling on a budget.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort. Relax with a cold Imperial beer (Costa Rica's iconic budget lager, approx $1–2 at a soda) and reflect on the day's experiences. Have dinner at your favorite local soda discovered during the trip.

meals.breakfast: Gallo pinto with natilla (sour cream) at a local soda — budget $3–5
meals.lunch: Packed lunch brought from the market — budget $4–6
meals.dinner: Whole fried fish with rice, beans, and salad at a beachside soda — budget $8–12

day_by_day.notes: Eco-reserves and biological stations often require advance reservations. Check their websites or ask your hotel to help book. Bring a notebook to jot down species you spot — it enhances the experience and helps with identification later.

day_by_day.morning: Morning horseback riding through the jungle or along the beach. Many local farms offer budget horseback tours for $25–45 USD for 2 hours. This is a fantastic way to cover more terrain and spot wildlife from an elevated vantage point while supporting local farming families.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a local organic farm or cacao plantation for a tour and tasting ($10–20 USD). Learn about sustainable agriculture in Costa Rica, see how chocolate is made from bean to bar, and taste fresh cacao pulp, chocolate, and local farm products.
day_by_day.evening: Cooking class or food tour in town if available ($20–30 USD for a group class). Learn to make traditional Costa Rican dishes like gallo pinto, ceviche, and tres leches cake. Alternatively, cook your own meal using ingredients from the local market.

meals.breakfast: Granola with fresh tropical fruit and yogurt — budget $4–6
meals.lunch: Farm-to-table snacks during the cacao/farm tour or packed lunch — budget $4–7
meals.dinner: Food from the cooking class or a local soda — budget $5–9

day_by_day.notes: Confirm horseback riding operator treats their horses humanely before booking — look for operators with small group sizes and well-maintained animals. The cacao tour typically includes all the chocolate you can taste, so arrive hungry!

day_by_day.morning: Final full-day adventure: White-water rafting on a nearby river OR a mangrove boat tour. White-water rafting on Class II–III rapids typically costs $45–65 USD with a reputable budget operator and includes all equipment. Mangrove boat tours are often cheaper ($20–35 USD) and excellent for wildlife — crocodiles, monkeys, and tropical birds.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the morning adventure, spend the afternoon at leisure on the beach. Swim, snorkel, or simply soak up the last full afternoon in Costa Rica. Visit any local spots you haven't yet explored.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner — splurge slightly on your last evening. Find a well-reviewed local restaurant (not a tourist trap) and enjoy a proper Costa Rican feast: fresh seafood, plantains, rice and beans, and a local dessert like tres leches or arroz con leche.

meals.breakfast: Big hearty breakfast before the rafting/boat tour — casado or eggs — budget $5–7
meals.lunch: Included with rafting tour OR fresh sandwich from a local bakery — budget $4–6
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at a local restaurant: seafood platter or mixed grill — budget $14–20

day_by_day.notes: For white-water rafting, ensure the operator provides certified guides, proper safety equipment (helmets, life jackets), and has a strong safety record. Don't raft if water levels are dangerously high after heavy rains. Book the mangrove tour for sunrise for the best wildlife activity.

day_by_day.morning: Wake up early for one last sunrise walk on the beach. Take final photos, collect any last souvenirs, and pack carefully. Check out of Aegean Bliss Resort. Store luggage with the hotel if your flight is later in the day.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on flight time, spend remaining hours at a nearby café or the beach. Head to Juan Santamaría International Airport via pre-booked shared shuttle (book the night before — approx $15–25 USD). Arrive at the airport at least 2.5–3 hours before your international flight.
day_by_day.evening: Board your departure flight. Reflect on 13 incredible days of eco-adventure, zip-lining, wildlife encounters, and authentic Costa Rican culture — all on a budget!

meals.breakfast: Final gallo pinto and coffee at a local soda near the hotel — budget $3–5
meals.lunch: Airport food or snacks packed from the supermarket — budget $5–10
meals.dinner: On the plane or airport restaurant

day_by_day.notes: Keep $29 USD in cash for the Costa Rica airport departure tax if not already included in your ticket (most modern tickets include it — verify with your airline). Do a final check of your room for any forgotten items: chargers, travel documents, medications. Take any leftover colones to exchange back or spend at the airport duty-free on local coffee or chocolate.

trip_options.title: Classic Costa Rica Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: N/A – Flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: N/A – In transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Juan Santamaría International Airport at 22:30. Clear customs and immigration, collect luggage, and arrange pre-booked private transfer or official airport taxi to your hotel. Check in to Aegean Bliss Resort and settle into your beachfront accommodation.

meals.breakfast: On the plane or at the airport
meals.lunch: On the plane or at the airport
meals.dinner: Light snack from the airport convenience store or 24-hour hotel room service upon arrival – keep it simple after a long travel day

day_by_day.notes: Pre-arrange your airport transfer before departure to avoid stress upon late-night arrival. Exchange a small amount of currency (USD is widely accepted in Costa Rica) at the airport for tips and incidentals. Set an alarm for a reasonable hour to begin adjusting to local time.

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and recover from travel. Enjoy a leisurely breakfast at the resort. Take a slow walk along the beachfront to orient yourself and soak in your first full Costa Rican morning. Visit the hotel concierge to confirm upcoming activity bookings and transportation logistics.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the immediate resort area and nearby town on foot or by bicycle rental. Visit a local farmers market or souvenir shop to pick up snacks and get a feel for the local culture. Relax on the beach and take a refreshing swim in the Pacific Ocean.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset stroll along the beach. Enjoy a welcome dinner at a well-regarded local restaurant near the resort to sample classic Costa Rican cuisine like gallo pinto, casado, and fresh ceviche.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast buffet – enjoy tropical fruits, eggs, and fresh-squeezed juice ($12–18 per person)
meals.lunch: Casual soda (local Costa Rican diner) near the resort – try a traditional casado plate with rice, beans, plantains, and your choice of protein ($8–12)
meals.dinner: Mid-range beachfront restaurant – fresh grilled fish, coconut shrimp, and a local Imperial beer or fresh agua de pipa (coconut water) ($20–30 per person)

day_by_day.notes: This is a deliberate rest and orientation day. Hydrate well, apply sunscreen, and avoid overexerting yourself after travel. Costa Rica is in the Central Time Zone (UTC-6). Tip culture is important – 10% service charge is standard, with an additional tip appreciated.

day_by_day.morning: Depart early by shuttle or private transfer toward Manuel Antonio National Park (approximately 30–45 minutes depending on resort location). Begin the Manuel Antonio National Park Guided Wildlife Hike at park opening (7:00 AM). A certified naturalist guide with a spotting scope will help you locate capuchin monkeys, sloths, poison dart frogs, scarlet macaws, and white-tailed deer in one of the world's most biodiverse parks.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the guided hike, relax on Playa Manuel Antonio inside the park – one of Costa Rica's most stunning beaches. Swim, snorkel, or simply observe the monkeys that frequent the shoreline. Exit the park by mid-afternoon and explore the town of Manuel Antonio for shopping and refreshments.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort by late afternoon. Freshen up and enjoy a relaxed dinner in the area. Watch for bioluminescence in the ocean after dark if conditions permit.

meals.breakfast: Early light breakfast at the resort or grab a 'boca' (small snack) from a local bakery en route – granola, fruit, and coffee ($5–10)
meals.lunch: Picnic lunch packed by the resort OR lunch at a soda just outside the park entrance – fresh fruit, sandwiches, and natural juice ($10–15)
meals.dinner: Dinner at a mid-range restaurant in Manuel Antonio town – try fresh tuna ceviche, arroz con mariscos (seafood rice), and a local craft beer ($22–32 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Book the Manuel Antonio guided hike in advance as entry numbers are capped. Wear lightweight, moisture-wicking clothing and waterproof hiking shoes. Bring insect repellent, sunscreen, and a reusable water bottle. Do not feed the wildlife – it is illegal and harmful to the animals.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning departure by shuttle or shared transport toward the Osa Peninsula (approximately 3–4 hours from Manuel Antonio area). This is a travel day, so enjoy the scenic Pacific coastal drive through small villages and lush jungle. Arrive at the gateway town of Puerto Jiménez or Drake Bay.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check in to a mid-range jungle lodge or eco-lodge in the Osa Peninsula area. After settling in, take a short introductory walk on a local trail near the lodge to spot toucans, scarlet macaws, and howler monkeys. Visit the town dock at Puerto Jiménez to arrange any final logistics for tomorrow's Corcovado expedition.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at the lodge or a local restaurant in Puerto Jiménez. Attend a brief orientation briefing by your expedition guide for tomorrow's Corcovado adventure. Early bedtime recommended.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast before departure – eggs, gallo pinto, tropical fruit, and coffee ($12–18)
meals.lunch: Roadside soda or lunch stop en route to Osa – typical casado or rice and bean dishes ($8–12)
meals.dinner: Dinner at a local eco-lodge restaurant in Puerto Jiménez – fresh catch of the day, hearts of palm salad, and plantain chips ($18–26 per person)

day_by_day.notes: The Osa Peninsula is remote and rugged – pack light but include rain gear, sturdy hiking boots, and a dry bag for electronics. February is generally dry season on the Osa, making it an excellent time to visit Corcovado. Cash is essential as ATMs are limited in this area.

day_by_day.morning: Full-day Osa Peninsula Corcovado Jungle Expedition & Snorkeling begins at dawn. Board a boat to reach the San Pedrillo or La Leona ranger station. Trek through Corcovado National Park's primary rainforest with an expert naturalist guide. Spot tapirs, white-lipped peccaries, jaguars (if incredibly lucky), giant anteaters, and an extraordinary array of birds including the harpy eagle.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the jungle trek, head to a pristine snorkeling spot in the Golfo Dulce or along the Osa coastline. Snorkel among colorful reef fish, sea turtles, and possibly dolphins. Enjoy a packed lunch on the beach in a truly remote paradise setting.
day_by_day.evening: Return by boat to Puerto Jiménez by late afternoon. Rest, shower, and enjoy a celebratory dinner reflecting on an extraordinary day in one of the world's most biodiverse places.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the lodge before 6:00 AM departure – eggs, fruit, coffee ($10–15)
meals.lunch: Packed lunch provided by the tour operator – sandwiches, fresh fruit, granola bars, and water (included in tour cost)
meals.dinner: Dinner at a local Osa restaurant – grilled fresh fish, patacones (fried plantains), rice and beans, and fresh lemonade ($20–28 per person)

day_by_day.notes: This is the most physically demanding day of the trip. Wear sturdy waterproof hiking boots and bring a change of clothes for snorkeling. Apply biodegradable sunscreen only. The Corcovado expedition must be booked well in advance with a licensed guide – solo entry is not permitted. Stay hydrated throughout the day.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely morning in the Osa Peninsula. Optional kayaking or stand-up paddleboarding in the calm waters of the Golfo Dulce. Spot dolphins that frequently visit the gulf in the early morning hours. Alternatively, relax at the lodge and journal about your Corcovado experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depart the Osa Peninsula by shuttle, small domestic flight (SANSA or Skyway), or 4x4 vehicle toward your next destination: Arenal Volcano area (approximately 6–7 hours by road or 1 hour by domestic flight + transfer). Domestic flight recommended for comfort and time savings. Arrive at Arenal and check in to a mid-range lodge with volcano views.
day_by_day.evening: Settle into your Arenal accommodation and enjoy the dramatic views of Arenal Volcano at dusk. Dinner at the lodge or a nearby restaurant in La Fortuna town.

meals.breakfast: Lodge breakfast in Osa – tropical fruits, eggs, local cheese, and coffee ($12–16)
meals.lunch: Airport café or roadside soda en route – light meal of empanadas, rice and beans, and fresh juice ($8–12)
meals.dinner: Dinner in La Fortuna – try a mid-range restaurant with volcano views, featuring wood-fired dishes, local trout, and fresh vegetables ($22–30 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Domestic flights in Costa Rica are affordable ($80–150 per person) and save significant travel time. Book SANSA or Skyway flights in advance. If driving, a 4x4 vehicle is strongly recommended. La Fortuna is the hub town for Arenal activities and has excellent mid-range dining and services.

day_by_day.morning: Begin the Arenal Volcano Hanging Bridges & Hot Springs experience. Start with the hanging bridges network at dawn when wildlife is most active. Walk through primary rainforest on 15+ suspension bridges offering breathtaking panoramic views of Arenal Volcano, Lake Arenal, and the surrounding jungle canopy. Spot poison dart frogs, toucans, morpho butterflies, and howler monkeys.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the hanging bridges, visit the Arenal 1968 Lava Trail – a short self-guided walk through the volcanic landscape created by the 1968 eruption. In the mid-afternoon, transition to the hot springs experience at one of the mid-range hot spring parks (Baldi or Tabacón area) – soak in naturally heated volcanic mineral pools surrounded by tropical gardens.
day_by_day.evening: Continue soaking in the hot springs as the sun sets and the volcano glows in the twilight. Enjoy dinner at the hot springs resort restaurant or return to La Fortuna for dinner.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the lodge before the hanging bridges – gallo pinto, eggs, and coffee ($12–16)
meals.lunch: Packed lunch or café at the hanging bridges visitor center – sandwiches, fresh fruit, and natural juice ($10–14)
meals.dinner: Dinner at a La Fortuna mid-range restaurant – try local trout (trucha) prepared in butter and garlic, served with rice, salad, and plantains ($20–28 per person)

day_by_day.notes: The hanging bridges are best experienced at sunrise – book the first entry slot. Wear layers as mornings near Arenal can be cool and misty. The hot springs are most atmospheric in the evening. Baldi Hot Springs offers a good mid-range option with multiple pools at varying temperatures. Bring a swimsuit and towel.

day_by_day.morning: Optional morning wildlife walk around Lake Arenal or on a local trail near your lodge. Look for caimans, herons, kingfishers, and Jesus Christ lizards (basilisks) along the lakeshore. Alternatively, book a morning kayaking or stand-up paddleboarding session on Lake Arenal with views of the volcano.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depart La Fortuna toward Monteverde (approximately 3–4 hours by road, including a scenic boat crossing of Lake Arenal followed by a 4x4 jeep transfer – the classic 'Jeep-Boat-Jeep' route). Arrive in Monteverde and check in to a mid-range cloud forest lodge. Explore the Santa Elena town area and visit a local artisan coffee shop.
day_by_day.evening: Visit a local cheese factory (COOP Monteverde is famous for its artisan cheeses) before it closes. Attend an optional night walk in the cloud forest to spot tree frogs, sleeping birds, and nocturnal insects with a guide.

meals.breakfast: Lodge breakfast in Arenal – full Costa Rican breakfast with tropical fruits, eggs, and fresh coffee ($12–16)
meals.lunch: Lunch during the Jeep-Boat-Jeep transfer – stop at a lakeside soda for casado or soup ($8–12)
meals.dinner: Dinner in Santa Elena, Monteverde – try a cozy mid-range café or restaurant featuring cloud forest-inspired dishes, local cheese platters, and homemade desserts ($18–26 per person)

day_by_day.notes: The Jeep-Boat-Jeep transfer is the most scenic and efficient way to travel from La Fortuna to Monteverde and costs approximately $25–35 per person. Book in advance through your lodge or a reputable operator. Roads into Monteverde are unpaved and bumpy – this is part of the adventure. The night walk must be booked in advance.

day_by_day.morning: The highlight of the Monteverde experience: Monteverde Cloud Forest Zip-Line Canopy Tour. Begin early with a safety briefing and gear-up session. Soar through the misty cloud forest canopy on one of Costa Rica's most thrilling zip-line circuits, featuring multiple cables, Tarzan swings, and rappelling sections. The cloud forest mist creates an ethereal, otherworldly atmosphere unlike any other zip-line experience in the country.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the adrenaline of zip-lining, visit the Monteverde Cloud Forest Biological Reserve or Santa Elena Cloud Forest Reserve for a self-guided or guided afternoon walk. Look for the resplendent quetzal (February is peak quetzal season!), three-wattled bellbirds, and dozens of orchid species. Visit the Monteverde Butterfly Garden or Frog Pond for additional wildlife encounters.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset views from a local café or lookout point above the cloud forest. Dinner in Santa Elena followed by optional live music at a local bar – Monteverde has a surprisingly vibrant small-town cultural scene.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the lodge before zip-lining – light meal of fruit, toast, and coffee ($10–14)
meals.lunch: Lunch at the zip-line operator's café or a nearby soda – casado, fresh juice, and tropical fruit ($10–15)
meals.dinner: Dinner at a well-regarded Monteverde restaurant – try wood-oven pizza, local cheese fondue, or a Costa Rican fusion dish paired with a glass of local guaro sour ($22–30 per person)

day_by_day.notes: February is one of the best months to spot the resplendent quetzal in Monteverde as it is quetzal breeding season. Hire a specialized quetzal guide for the afternoon walk to maximize your chances. The zip-line tour lasts approximately 3–4 hours. Wear closed-toe shoes and comfortable clothes that can get muddy. The cloud forest is cool and often misty – bring a light rain jacket.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning guided bird-watching walk in the cloud forest with a local ornithologist guide. The cloud forest at dawn is extraordinarily alive with bird song and activity. Look for emerald toucanets, golden-browed chlorophonias, and the iconic resplendent quetzal. Visit the Hummingbird Gallery near the cloud forest reserve entrance – dozens of hummingbird species feed at the garden feeders.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Monteverde Cheese Factory for a tour and tasting. Explore local artisan shops and purchase handmade crafts, locally produced coffee, and chocolate. In the afternoon, visit the Selvatura Adventure Park for the hanging bridges walkway (different perspective from Arenal) or the reptile and amphibian exhibition.
day_by_day.evening: Depart Monteverde toward the Pacific coast via shuttle to return to the Aegean Bliss Resort (approximately 3–4 hours). Arrive at the resort in the evening and enjoy a welcome-back dinner celebrating your cloud forest adventures.

meals.breakfast: Early lodge breakfast before bird-watching – gallo pinto, eggs, local cheese, and coffee ($12–16)
meals.lunch: Cheese factory café lunch – artisan cheese platter, fresh bread, local jam, and coffee ($12–18)
meals.dinner: Welcome-back dinner at the resort restaurant or a favorite local beachfront spot – fresh seafood, cold beer, and tropical dessert ($22–30 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Arrange your shuttle from Monteverde back to the coast in advance through your lodge. The road from Monteverde to the Pan-American Highway is unpaved – shared shuttle services handle this comfortably. Store any artisan purchases carefully in your luggage. This is a transition day back to the beach for the final days of the trip.

day_by_day.morning: Depart very early by private transfer or shuttle toward Tortuguero on the Caribbean coast (approximately 4–5 hours from San José area, or arrange via a Tortuguero package that includes boat transfer from Caño Blanco or Moín). Arrive in Tortuguero – a car-free village accessible only by boat or plane. Check in to a mid-range eco-lodge along the canal.
day_by_day.afternoon: Begin the Tortuguero National Park Wildlife Boat Safari in the afternoon. Board a covered motorized canoe with a certified naturalist guide and navigate the jungle waterways and canals of Tortuguero. Spot caimans sunning on logs, river otters, Jesus Christ lizards, poison dart frogs, green iguanas, and an incredible diversity of waterbirds including anhingas, kingfishers, and tiger herons.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the eco-lodge for dinner. Enjoy a quiet evening listening to the sounds of the jungle – howler monkeys, frogs, and tropical insects create a remarkable natural symphony. Optional night canal tour to spot caimans and nocturnal wildlife by spotlight.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the resort before departure – light and portable ($10–14)
meals.lunch: Lunch at a Tortuguero village soda or eco-lodge upon arrival – rice, beans, fresh fish, and plantains ($10–15)
meals.dinner: Dinner at the eco-lodge – Caribbean-style cuisine featuring coconut rice and beans, jerk chicken or fresh snook fish, and tropical fruit juice ($18–26 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Tortuguero is logistically complex to reach – book a package through a reputable operator that includes boat transfers from the mainland. February is dry season on the Pacific but the Caribbean side can receive some rain year-round – pack a compact rain poncho. Tortuguero is famous for sea turtle nesting (July–October) but the wildlife boat safari is spectacular year-round. Mosquito repellent is essential.

day_by_day.morning: Second Tortuguero Wildlife Boat Safari at dawn – the early morning hours offer the best wildlife sightings as animals are most active. Paddle by kayak or canoe through narrower jungle channels for a quieter, more intimate wildlife experience. Look for West Indian manatees in the deeper canals, spider monkeys in the canopy, and spectacular tropical birds.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Tortuguero village on foot – visit the Sea Turtle Conservancy visitor center to learn about the park's conservation history and the famous sea turtle nesting programs. Browse local artisan shops and enjoy a slow Caribbean afternoon. Return to the mainland by boat transfer and arrange private transfer back to the Aegean Bliss Resort (arriving evening).
day_by_day.evening: Arrive back at the Aegean Bliss Resort. Enjoy a relaxed farewell dinner at the resort, reflecting on the incredible diversity of ecosystems and wildlife encountered throughout the trip.

meals.breakfast: Early eco-lodge breakfast before the dawn safari – fruit, toast, eggs, and Caribbean coffee ($10–14)
meals.lunch: Lunch at a Tortuguero village restaurant – Caribbean rice and beans (made with coconut milk), fresh fish, and cold drink ($10–15)
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at the Aegean Bliss Resort restaurant – splurge slightly on a special seafood platter, tropical cocktails, and a decadent dessert ($28–40 per person)

day_by_day.notes: The dawn kayak safari requires an early 5:30 AM start – arrange with your eco-lodge the night before. The return journey from Tortuguero involves a boat to the mainland followed by a road transfer – this can take 3–4 hours total. Confirm your transfer timing with your operator. This is your penultimate night – pack non-essential items in the evening.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning at the Aegean Bliss Resort. Enjoy a leisurely last breakfast on the beachfront terrace. Take one final swim in the Pacific Ocean and a slow walk along the beach to collect memories (and perhaps a few shells). Visit the resort spa for a relaxing massage or treatment as a final luxury before departure.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out of the resort and arrange private transfer to Juan Santamaría International Airport in San José (travel time varies by resort location – typically 2–4 hours; confirm timing based on your flight). Arrive at the airport with ample time for check-in, security, and duty-free shopping. Pick up last-minute souvenirs including locally grown coffee, chocolate, and artisan goods at the airport shops.
day_by_day.evening: Depart Costa Rica with extraordinary memories of cloud forests, volcanoes, jungle waterways, and some of the most biodiverse wildlife on Earth. Pura Vida!

meals.breakfast: Final resort breakfast – make it special with fresh tropical fruits, a full Costa Rican spread, and a perfect cup of local coffee ($14–20)
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the airport or a quick stop at a local soda en route – empanadas, fresh juice, and a snack ($8–12)
meals.dinner: Airport restaurant or on the plane

day_by_day.notes: Check your flight departure time carefully and allow at least 3 hours before your international flight for check-in and security at Juan Santamaría Airport. Confirm your airport transfer the night before. Costa Rica charges an airport departure tax (currently included in most airline tickets but verify). Declare any food items at customs. Consider purchasing vacuum-sealed Costa Rican coffee at the airport as a perfect souvenir – it is allowed through customs in most countries.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Costa Rica Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

experiences.name: Monteverde Cloud Forest Zip-Line Canopy Tour
experiences.description: Soar through the misty cloud forest canopy on one of Costa Rica's most thrilling zip-line circuits. With over 13 cables and Tarzan swings, you'll glide above the treetops spotting howler monkeys, toucans, and exotic orchids while experienced guides share insights about the unique cloud forest ecosystem.

experiences.name: Tortuguero National Park Wildlife Boat Safari
experiences.description: Navigate the jungle waterways of Tortuguero by boat with a naturalist guide to spot caimans, river otters, manatees, three-toed sloths, and hundreds of bird species. If visiting between July and October, witness the awe-inspiring nesting of green sea turtles on the black-sand beaches at night.

experiences.name: Arenal Volcano Hanging Bridges & Hot Springs
experiences.description: Trek through primary rainforest on a network of suspension bridges offering panoramic views of Arenal Volcano and its surrounding wildlife. Spot poison dart frogs, coatis, and morpho butterflies by day, then unwind in natural volcanic hot spring pools fed by geothermal activity as the jungle comes alive at dusk.

experiences.name: Manuel Antonio National Park Guided Wildlife Hike
experiences.description: Explore one of the world's most biodiverse national parks with a certified naturalist guide equipped with a high-powered spotting scope. Encounter white-faced capuchin monkeys, two-toed sloths, scarlet macaws, and iguanas along jungle trails that open onto pristine white-sand beaches with turquoise Pacific waters.

experiences.name: Osa Peninsula Corcovado Jungle Expedition & Snorkeling
experiences.description: Venture into Corcovado National Park, dubbed by National Geographic as the most biologically intense place on Earth. Hike remote trails with a ranger guide to spot tapirs, peccaries, and harpy eagles, then snorkel the coral reefs of Caño Island teeming with sea turtles, reef sharks, and manta rays in the warm Pacific waters.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — late-night arrival
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities scheduled — late-night arrival
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Juan Santamaría International Airport at 22:30 on Flight UA. A private luxury transfer will be waiting to whisk you to Aegean Bliss Resort. Upon arrival, enjoy a welcome cocktail and a light late-night amenity tray prepared by the resort. Check in, unwind, and settle into your beachfront suite.

meals.breakfast: Not applicable — in-flight or airport dining
meals.lunch: Not applicable — in-flight or airport dining
meals.dinner: Late-night welcome amenity tray at the resort (charcuterie, tropical fruits, artisan chocolates, and sparkling wine) arranged by the concierge

day_by_day.notes: Private airport transfer should be pre-arranged. Confirm check-in details with the resort in advance. Request a turndown service and early breakfast reservation for the following morning to ease into the trip.

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and enjoy a leisurely beachfront breakfast. After breakfast, take a private resort orientation tour — explore the grounds, spa facilities, pool areas, and beachfront. Spend time acclimatizing with a gentle morning yoga session on the beach deck offered by the resort's wellness team.
day_by_day.afternoon: Embark on a private snorkeling excursion arranged by the resort along the nearby Pacific coastline. Explore vibrant coral reefs and spot tropical marine life including parrotfish, angelfish, and sea turtles. Return to the resort for a relaxing afternoon by the infinity pool with personalized poolside service.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails at the resort's ocean-view bar, followed by a romantic beachfront dinner under the stars at the resort's signature fine-dining restaurant, featuring fresh Costa Rican seafood and farm-to-table cuisine.

meals.breakfast: Full gourmet breakfast at the resort's beachfront restaurant — tropical fruit platters, freshly baked pastries, eggs Benedict with smoked marlin, and Costa Rican specialty coffee
meals.lunch: Light poolside lunch — ceviche, grilled shrimp skewers, fresh coconut, and tropical juices
meals.dinner: Signature beachfront restaurant at Aegean Bliss Resort — multi-course tasting menu featuring locally sourced seafood, hearts of palm salad, and a decadent passion fruit soufflé for dessert

day_by_day.notes: This is a gentle recovery and orientation day after the late arrival. Confirm all upcoming excursion bookings with the concierge today and arrange any necessary private transfers for the days ahead.

day_by_day.morning: Depart early by private vehicle for Manuel Antonio National Park (approximately 20–40 minutes depending on resort location). Begin the Manuel Antonio National Park Guided Wildlife Hike with a certified naturalist guide equipped with high-powered telescopes and binoculars. Spot three-toed sloths, white-faced capuchin monkeys, scarlet macaws, and the elusive Jesus Christ lizard along pristine jungle trails.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the guided hike, enjoy a private beach picnic lunch at one of Manuel Antonio's stunning secluded coves. Spend the early afternoon swimming in the crystal-clear waters of the park's protected beach. Return to the resort by mid-afternoon for a relaxing spa treatment — book the resort's signature volcanic stone massage.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at a premium restaurant in the Manuel Antonio area, or return to the resort for a private chef's table experience with a curated Costa Rican tasting menu.

meals.breakfast: Early gourmet breakfast at the resort before departure — avocado toast with local microgreens, tropical smoothie bowls, and specialty coffee
meals.lunch: Gourmet private picnic lunch prepared by the resort — artisan sandwiches, fresh tropical fruit, local cheeses, sparkling water, and chilled white wine served in the national park
meals.dinner: La Luna Restaurant (Manuel Antonio area) — renowned for its stunning ocean views and sophisticated Costa Rican fusion cuisine, or private chef's table at Aegean Bliss Resort

day_by_day.notes: Manuel Antonio National Park has a daily visitor cap, so entry reservations must be secured well in advance. Wear comfortable hiking shoes, apply reef-safe sunscreen, and bring insect repellent. The naturalist guide will carry the optical equipment.

day_by_day.morning: Begin a full-day journey to the Osa Peninsula for the Corcovado Jungle Expedition & Snorkeling experience. Depart the resort early by private vehicle or arrange a scenic small-plane charter for a breathtaking aerial arrival over the Osa Peninsula. Enter Corcovado National Park — dubbed by National Geographic as the most biologically intense place on Earth — with an expert naturalist guide.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the Corcovado expedition into the afternoon. Trek through primary rainforest teeming with tapirs, jaguars (rare but possible), giant anteaters, harpy eagles, and poison dart frogs. Transition to a guided snorkeling session in the warm Pacific waters off the Osa coastline, where whale sharks, manta rays, and hawksbill sea turtles are frequently encountered.
day_by_day.evening: Return transfer to the resort (by charter flight or private vehicle). Enjoy a restorative dinner at the resort, celebrating the day's extraordinary wildlife encounters.

meals.breakfast: Early pre-departure breakfast at the resort — energy-rich selections including granola, eggs, fresh fruit, and coffee
meals.lunch: Gourmet packed lunch provided by the tour operator or resort, enjoyed in a jungle clearing within Corcovado — local rice and bean wraps, fresh fruit, energy bars, and hydration packs
meals.dinner: Resort signature restaurant — celebrate the day with a premium surf-and-turf dinner: grilled local catch of the day, tenderloin with chimichurri, and a curated Costa Rican wine selection

day_by_day.notes: Corcovado requires advance permits and must be entered with a certified guide. The charter flight option (approximately 45 minutes vs. 4+ hours by road) is highly recommended for this luxury itinerary. Wear long sleeves and pants for jungle trekking. Bring waterproof bags for electronics.

day_by_day.morning: A well-deserved rest and rejuvenation morning. Begin with a private sunrise paddleboard or kayak session along the calm beachfront waters. Follow with a 90-minute couples' or solo spa treatment at the resort's luxury wellness center — choose from a rainforest botanical wrap, deep tissue massage, or hydrotherapy circuit.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private guided birdwatching walk along the resort's surrounding coastal forests and estuary. Costa Rica's Pacific coast is home to scarlet macaws, toucans, and over 200 species of birds easily spotted from the resort's environs. Spend the late afternoon relaxing at the pool with a curated selection of cocktails and light snacks.
day_by_day.evening: Private beachfire dinner experience — the resort sets up an exclusive beachfront table with tiki torches, a personal butler, and a bespoke menu prepared by the executive chef. Pair with a sommelier-selected wine flight.

meals.breakfast: In-room breakfast delivered to your suite terrace — eggs any style, fresh-pressed juices, tropical fruit, pastries, and a French press of single-origin Costa Rican coffee
meals.lunch: Poolside gourmet spread — fresh ceviche bar, grilled octopus, lobster bisque, and a chilled rosé
meals.dinner: Exclusive private beachfire dinner — five-course bespoke menu including lobster thermidor, wagyu beef tenderloin, and a decadent chocolate and coffee lava cake

day_by_day.notes: This is a planned recovery day after the intensive Corcovado expedition. Use this day to confirm and finalize logistics for the upcoming multi-day journey to Arenal and Monteverde. The concierge should arrange private transportation for Day 6.

day_by_day.morning: Depart the resort after breakfast for the journey to the Arenal Volcano region (approximately 3–4 hours by private luxury vehicle, or consider a scenic domestic charter flight). Enjoy the lush landscapes en route. Check in to a premium eco-lodge or luxury resort near Arenal Volcano — request a suite with a direct volcano view.
day_by_day.afternoon: Begin the Arenal Volcano Hanging Bridges experience — trek through primary rainforest on a network of suspension bridges offering panoramic views of the majestic Arenal Volcano. Spot howler monkeys, toucans, morpho butterflies, and coatis along the trail. A private naturalist guide enhances every sighting with expert commentary.
day_by_day.evening: Soak in the famous Arenal natural hot springs at a premium private hot spring resort (such as Tabacón or Baldi) — enjoy thermal pools of varying temperatures surrounded by lush jungle. Dine at the hot springs resort's gourmet restaurant overlooking the illuminated volcano.

meals.breakfast: Final breakfast at Aegean Bliss Resort — full gourmet spread to fuel the travel day
meals.lunch: Gourmet lunch stop en route to Arenal at a premium restaurant in San José or the Central Valley — traditional Costa Rican casado elevated with premium ingredients, fresh ceviche, and local craft beer or wine
meals.dinner: Tabacón Grand Spa Thermal Resort Restaurant (or equivalent) — romantic jungle dining with views of the volcano, featuring a menu of Costa Rican-inspired gourmet cuisine including palm heart salad, sea bass in plantain crust, and tres leches cake

day_by_day.notes: Book the Arenal luxury lodge in advance and confirm volcano-view suite availability. The hanging bridges are best explored in the early afternoon before afternoon mist rolls in. Hot springs reservations at Tabacón should be pre-booked, especially during peak season.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning private guided wildlife walk around the Arenal area — the forests surrounding the volcano are exceptionally active at dawn. Spot poison dart frogs, Jesus Christ lizards, three-toed sloths, and a spectacular array of tropical birds. Return to the lodge for a leisurely breakfast.
day_by_day.afternoon: Optional adventure activity in the Arenal area — choose from white-water rafting on the Balsa River (Class III–IV rapids), a private horseback ride through the rainforest to a hidden waterfall, or a guided kayaking tour on Lake Arenal with stunning volcano views. Spend the late afternoon relaxing at the lodge's infinity pool.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the hot springs for a twilight soak, followed by a private in-lodge dinner prepared by a personal chef — a curated Costa Rican tasting menu featuring local ingredients sourced from nearby farms.

meals.breakfast: Lodge breakfast — fresh tropical fruits, gallo pinto (traditional Costa Rican rice and beans), farm eggs, local cheese, and specialty coffee from the Arenal region
meals.lunch: Lakeside lunch at a premium restaurant on the shores of Lake Arenal — grilled freshwater fish, plantain chips, and fresh lemonade with mint
meals.dinner: Private chef's dinner at the lodge — five-course farm-to-table tasting menu with local cheeses, heart of palm soup, grilled tenderloin, and a dessert of local chocolate fondue with tropical fruits

day_by_day.notes: The white-water rafting option requires a moderate fitness level. Horseback riding is suitable for all levels and offers one of the most scenic ways to explore the area. Confirm the afternoon activity preference with the concierge the night before.

day_by_day.morning: Depart Arenal after breakfast for the journey to Monteverde (approximately 2.5–3 hours by private vehicle via the scenic Lake Arenal road — one of Costa Rica's most breathtaking drives). Check in to a premium eco-lodge in Monteverde — request a suite with cloud forest views. After settling in, take a short orientation walk on the lodge's private reserve trails.
day_by_day.afternoon: Afternoon visit to the Santa Elena Cloud Forest Reserve or Monteverde Cloud Forest Biological Reserve for a private guided walk. Discover the mystical cloud forest draped in mosses and orchids, home to the resplendent quetzal, emerald toucanets, and glass frogs. A private guide maximizes wildlife sightings.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a premium night tour of the cloud forest — experience the magical nocturnal world of Monteverde, spotting tarantulas, kinkajous, sleeping birds, and bioluminescent fungi with expert guidance. Return to the lodge for a warming dinner.

meals.breakfast: Final breakfast at the Arenal lodge — hearty spread to fuel the travel day, including tropical smoothies, eggs, and local pastries
meals.lunch: Lunch stop en route to Monteverde at a charming premium restaurant in the small town of Tilarán — fresh tilapia, local vegetables, and artisan bread
meals.dinner: Monteverde lodge restaurant — warming cloud forest cuisine featuring mushroom risotto with local fungi, roasted chicken with chimichurri, and a selection of Costa Rican craft beers and wines

day_by_day.notes: The drive along Lake Arenal is spectacular — request a brief stop at a scenic viewpoint. Monteverde's cloud forest is cool and misty year-round; pack a light waterproof jacket and layers. Night tours require advance booking and are limited in group size.

day_by_day.morning: The highlight of Monteverde — the Monteverde Cloud Forest Zip-Line Canopy Tour. Soar through the misty cloud forest canopy on one of Costa Rica's most thrilling zip-line circuits, with cables stretching up to 1 km and platforms nestled high in the forest canopy. The experience includes Tarzan swings, rappelling, and breathtaking views of the Gulf of Nicoya on clear days. A private or small-group VIP experience is recommended.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the adrenaline rush, enjoy a tranquil afternoon at the Monteverde Butterfly Garden and Hummingbird Gallery — a serene contrast to the morning's adventure. Watch dozens of hummingbird species feed just inches away. Visit the Orchid Garden, home to over 400 orchid species. Enjoy a relaxing afternoon at the lodge's spa.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner in Monteverde at a premium restaurant, celebrating the cloud forest experience. Prepare for the journey to Tortuguero the following day.

meals.breakfast: Early energizing breakfast at the lodge — protein-rich selections including eggs, yogurt parfaits, granola, and fresh fruit to prepare for the zip-line adventure
meals.lunch: Post-zip-line lunch at a premium Monteverde restaurant — try the local specialty of chayote soup, followed by a grilled sea bass with tropical salsa
meals.dinner: Sofia Restaurant (Monteverde) or equivalent premium dining — acclaimed for its nuevo Latino cuisine featuring local ingredients, craft cocktails, and an impressive dessert menu with local chocolate creations

day_by_day.notes: The zip-line tour typically has weight limits (check in advance). Closed-toe shoes are mandatory. GoPro cameras can often be rented on-site for capturing the experience. Book the VIP or private zip-line experience well in advance to secure preferred morning slots.

day_by_day.morning: Depart Monteverde after an early breakfast for the journey to Tortuguero on the Caribbean coast (approximately 5–6 hours by private vehicle and boat transfer, or consider a domestic charter flight to save time). The boat journey through jungle canals to reach Tortuguero is itself a wildlife experience — spot caimans, river otters, and tropical birds en route.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at a premium eco-lodge in Tortuguero (accessible only by boat or small plane). Check in and settle into your jungle lodge suite. After resting, take a short afternoon guided walk on the lodge's private trails to begin spotting the incredible Caribbean wildlife.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a welcome dinner at the lodge, followed by an optional evening stroll along the beach — Tortuguero is world-famous for sea turtle nesting (February may offer early-season sightings of leatherback turtles with appropriate permits and guidance).

meals.breakfast: Early departure breakfast at the Monteverde lodge — packed to-go option or quick hot breakfast before the journey
meals.lunch: Lunch en route — stop at a premium restaurant in the Caribbean lowlands, sampling the distinctive Afro-Caribbean cuisine of Costa Rica's Caribbean coast: rice and beans cooked in coconut milk, jerk chicken, and fresh patacones
meals.dinner: Lodge restaurant in Tortuguero — Caribbean-inspired cuisine featuring coconut shrimp, plantain-crusted snapper, and a rum-based tropical dessert

day_by_day.notes: The journey to Tortuguero is part of the adventure. Confirm whether the charter flight or road-and-boat transfer is preferred — the flight is far more efficient. Pack light for Tortuguero as luggage is transported by boat. Humidity is high on the Caribbean coast; pack accordingly.

day_by_day.morning: Embark on the Tortuguero National Park Wildlife Boat Safari — navigate the jungle waterways by private boat with an expert naturalist guide. Glide silently through the labyrinthine canals spotting spectacled caimans basking on riverbanks, river otters playing in the current, great green macaws, roseate spoonbills, and troops of howler and spider monkeys. The early morning light creates extraordinary photography opportunities.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the lodge for a leisurely lunch. Spend the afternoon on a kayaking tour through the smaller secondary canals of Tortuguero — a more intimate wildlife experience accessible only by non-motorized craft. Spot basilisk lizards, tree frogs, and an incredible diversity of waterbirds up close.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset boat tour along the main Tortuguero canal, followed by a premium lodge dinner. If sea turtle nesting activity is confirmed, join a guided nighttime beach walk (strictly regulated and guided) to witness the awe-inspiring spectacle of nesting leatherback sea turtles.

meals.breakfast: Early lodge breakfast before the boat safari — fresh tropical fruits, eggs, gallo pinto, Caribbean-style bread pudding, and specialty coffee
meals.lunch: Lodge lunch — Caribbean lobster salad, coconut soup, and fresh lemonade
meals.dinner: Premium lodge dinner — whole grilled Caribbean snapper, plantain gnocchi, and a decadent chocolate and coconut tart, paired with a curated wine selection

day_by_day.notes: The morning boat safari should depart at first light (approximately 5:30–6:00 AM) for the best wildlife activity. Sea turtle nesting beach walks are strictly regulated by park authorities — only certified guides may lead these tours, and photography is restricted to protect the turtles. Confirm turtle activity with the lodge in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Tortuguero — enjoy a sunrise walk along the deserted black-sand beach with a naturalist guide. Watch for early-morning bird activity including kingfishers, herons, and the magnificent great green macaw. Return to the lodge for a leisurely farewell breakfast.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depart Tortuguero by charter flight or boat-and-vehicle transfer back toward the Pacific coast or San José area. Check in to a premium San José area hotel or return to Aegean Bliss Resort (if itinerary routing allows) for the final night. Use the afternoon to visit the Gold Museum or Jade Museum in San José for a cultural immersion, or simply relax at the hotel.
day_by_day.evening: Celebratory farewell dinner at one of San José's finest restaurants — a fitting conclusion to an extraordinary 13-day Costa Rican adventure.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely farewell breakfast at the Tortuguero lodge — full spread with Caribbean specialties, freshly squeezed juices, and artisan coffee
meals.lunch: Light lunch en route or upon arrival at the San José hotel — fresh ceviche, empanadas, and tropical fruit
meals.dinner: Restaurante Grano de Oro (San José) or equivalent — one of Costa Rica's most celebrated fine-dining establishments, set in a beautifully restored Victorian mansion, featuring a sophisticated Costa Rican-European fusion menu and an exceptional wine cellar

day_by_day.notes: Confirm the return transfer logistics with the concierge. If flying out of Juan Santamaría Airport the following day, choose a hotel within 20–30 minutes of the airport for convenience. Request a wake-up call and early breakfast for the departure morning.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Costa Rica. Enjoy a leisurely breakfast at the hotel. Use the morning for last-minute souvenir shopping — visit a premium artisan market or boutique for locally made coffee, dark chocolate, hand-painted ceramics, and sustainable jewelry crafted by Costa Rican artisans.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on flight time, enjoy a final swim, spa treatment, or coffee tasting experience at the hotel. Complete final packing and check out. Private luxury transfer to Juan Santamaría International Airport. Arrive at the airport with ample time for premium check-in and lounge access.
